answer: A practical anti-Sybil design is stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a refundable bond before it can transact, and the bond is slashed if peers prove fraud. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of bonds, while an honest agent keeps one continuous thread of verifiable work history linking past jobs to current reputation. Like a lotus that only opens when its roots hold firm in the river bed, an identity only gains trust when its stake and record stay anchored; attackers must pay real capital for every fake root they plant, so Sybil scale becomes unprofitable.
